metadata.title: Total RNA Extraction with TRIzol Reagent
metadata.purpose: Isolate high-quality total RNA from cells or tissue using TRIzol Reagent by acid guanidinium/phenol-chloroform phase separation followed by isopropanol precipitation, an ethanol wash, and resuspension for downstream use (RT-PCR, Northern blot, etc.).
metadata.scope: Single-step total RNA isolation from human, animal, plant, yeast, or bacterial cells and tissues with TRIzol Reagent (Cat. no. 15596026). Covers only the RNA arm; sequential DNA/protein recovery from the interphase/organic phase is out of scope here.
beforeYouBegin: Work RNase-free: wear gloves and change them frequently, use sterile RNase-free plasticware and tips, and decontaminate surfaces (e.g. RNaseZap).
Process samples immediately after collection, or flash-freeze and store at -80 C until extraction.
The sample volume added should not exceed 25% of the TRIzol volume used for lysis. Perform all steps at 20-25 C unless noted.

materials.name: TRIzol Reagent
materials.specification: Monophasic solution of phenol and guanidine isothiocyanate; ready-to-use
materials.hazard: Contains phenol and guanidine isothiocyanate; toxic and corrosive - use in a fume hood, avoid skin/eye contact
materials.rawText: TRIzol Reagent is a monophasic solution of phenol, guanidine isothiocyanate, and other proprietary components

materials.name: Chloroform
materials.workingConcentration: 0.2 mL per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis
materials.hazard: Toxic, volatile - use in a fume hood
materials.rawText: Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis

materials.name: Isopropanol
materials.workingConcentration: 0.5 mL per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis
materials.rawText: Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase, per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis

materials.name: Ethanol, 75%
materials.workingConcentration: 1 mL per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis
materials.rawText: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis

materials.name: RNase-free water
materials.specification: Or 0.1 mM EDTA, or 0.5% SDS (do not use SDS if the RNA will be used in enzymatic reactions); 20-50 uL to resuspend
materials.rawText: Resuspend the pellet in 20-50 uL of RNase-free water, 0.1 mM EDTA, or 0.5% SDS solution

materials.name: RNase-free glycogen
materials.specification: Optional carrier for small samples (<10^6 cells or <10 mg tissue); co-precipitates with RNA without interfering downstream
materials.rawText: add 5-10 ug of RNase-free glycogen as a carrier to the aqueous phase

equipment.name: Refrigerated microcentrifuge
equipment.model: Capable of 12,000 x g at 4 C
equipment.settings: 12,000 x g, 4 C (phase separation and precipitation); 7500 x g, 4 C (ethanol wash)

samples.name: Cells or tissue
samples.description: 50-100 mg tissue, or 1x10^5-1x10^7 monolayer cells, or 5-10x10^6 (animal/plant/yeast) or 1x10^7 (bacterial) suspension cells, per 1 mL TRIzol.

samples.name: Aqueous phase
samples.description: Colorless upper phase containing RNA, recovered after chloroform phase separation.

samples.name: Total RNA
samples.description: Purified total RNA resuspended in RNase-free water; A260/A280 ~2 when pure.

tables.title: Starting material per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent
tables.note: Sample volume should not exceed 25% of the TRIzol volume used for lysis.

steps.action: Lyse and homogenize the sample in TRIzol Reagent according to starting material (1 mL TRIzol per 50-100 mg tissue, per 1x10^5-1x10^7 monolayer cells, or per 0.25 mL suspension cells). Pipette or homogenize until homogeneous.

parameters.rawText: Add 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent per 50-100 mg of tissue

steps.criticalNotes: Do not wash cells before adding TRIzol (avoids mRNA degradation). Sample volume must not exceed 25% of the TRIzol volume.

steps.action: (Optional, high-fat samples) Centrifuge the lysate 5 min at 12,000 x g, 4-10 C, and transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.
Incubate 5 min to allow complete dissociation of the nucleoprotein complexes.
Add 0.2 mL chloroform per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis, securely cap the tube, and mix thoroughly by shaking.

parameters.rawText: Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent

steps.action: Centrifuge 15 min at 12,000 x g, 4 C. The mixture separates into a lower phenol-chloroform phase, an interphase, and a colorless upper aqueous phase.
steps.expectedResult: Three phases; RNA is in the colorless upper aqueous phase.

steps.action: Transfer the aqueous phase (containing RNA) to a new tube by angling the tube at 45 degrees and pipetting; avoid the interphase and organic layer.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not carry over any interphase or organic phase, which would contaminate the RNA with DNA/protein.

steps.action: (Optional, small samples) Add 5-10 ug RNase-free glycogen as a carrier. Then add 0.5 mL isopropanol to the aqueous phase per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis.

parameters.rawText: Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase, per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent

steps.action: Incubate 10 min at room temperature (15-30 C).
Centrifuge 10 min at 12,000 x g, 4 C. RNA forms a white gel-like pellet at the bottom of the tube. Discard the supernatant with a micropipettor.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL TRIzol used for lysis.

parameters.rawText: 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent

steps.criticalNotes: RNA can be stored in 75% ethanol at -20 C for at least 1 year (or 4 C for at least 1 week).

steps.action: Vortex the sample briefly, then centrifuge 5 min at 7500 x g, 4 C; discard the supernatant with a micropipettor.
Vacuum or air dry the RNA pellet for 5-10 min. Do not dry by vacuum centrifuge and do not let the pellet dry completely.
steps.criticalNotes: Over-dried pellets dissolve poorly; partially dissolved RNA gives A230/280 < 1.6.

steps.action: Resuspend the pellet in 20-50 uL of RNase-free water (or 0.1 mM EDTA, or 0.5% SDS) by pipetting up and down.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not use 0.5% SDS if the RNA will be used in subsequent enzymatic reactions (e.g. reverse transcription).

steps.action: Incubate in a water bath or heat block at 55-60 C for 10-15 min to fully dissolve the RNA.
steps.criticalNotes: Proceed to downstream applications or store the RNA at -70 C.

steps.action: Determine RNA yield and purity by absorbance: measure A260 and A280, calculate concentration as A260 x dilution x 40 = ug RNA/mL, and compute the A260/A280 ratio (~2 = pure).

branches.action: Suspect protein/phenol carryover; re-precipitate or repeat the 75% ethanol wash before use.

steps.expectedResult: A260/A280 ratio of ~2 indicates pure RNA.

expectedOutputs: Purified total RNA in RNase-free water with an A260/A280 ratio of ~2.
Yields in the typical ranges listed in the yields table (e.g. 6-10 ug per mg of liver).

troubleshooting.cause: Incomplete homogenization; loss of aqueous phase; pellet over-dried and not fully dissolved
troubleshooting.solution: Homogenize thoroughly; recover the full aqueous phase without the interphase; do not over-dry; solubilize at 55-60 C

troubleshooting.cause: Protein or phenol carryover from the interphase/organic phase
troubleshooting.solution: Avoid the interphase during transfer; repeat the 75% ethanol wash; re-precipitate

troubleshooting.cause: Pellet dried too much / RNA only partially dissolved
troubleshooting.solution: Do not fully dry the pellet; extend solubilization time at 55-60 C

troubleshooting.cause: Interphase carryover; genomic DNA in aqueous phase
troubleshooting.solution: Treat with DNase I (Amplification Grade) before downstream enzymatic steps

safety: TRIzol contains phenol and guanidine isothiocyanate - toxic and corrosive; wear gloves, eye protection, and lab coat and work in a fume hood.
Chloroform and isopropanol are volatile and hazardous; handle in a fume hood and dispose of organic waste per institutional rules.
Guanidine isothiocyanate forms reactive/toxic products with bleach - do not mix TRIzol waste with hypochlorite.
limitations: Phenol/guanidinium chemistry co-purifies small RNAs but is prone to phenol carryover (low A260/A230) and requires careful phase handling. Does not remove genomic DNA (add a DNase step if needed). Yields and sample-input amounts must be adjusted to the specific tissue/cell type.
